question: Resolve the 224 tail CFs whose Form 990 fee line has no stated base ('ADMINISTRATIVE FEES' etc.): their visible fee ÷ total assets is bimodal (103 under 20 bps, 94 at 50 bps or more). For the 94 at 50+ bps, read Schedule O and Part IX expense detail, or a posted audit where robots allow, to decide whether the line is the internal fee charged to component funds; re-run the realised-rate pool with the reclassified set
conclusion_affected: Realised CF pool central $49.4m and its band medians (n = 13/18/10 complete-capture CFs)
rationale: Only 47 of 641 tail CFs (7%) are classed internal from wording; the 94 high-rate unknowns could triple the observed set and tighten the band medians

question: DAF-specific realised fee at internal-fee tail CFs: for the 41 complete-capture internal-fee CFs, find fund-type detail (audit notes on fee by fund type, posted fee policies, Schedule D Part V split) to estimate the DAF rate relative to the all-fund rate; apply the ratio to convert the $49.4m all-fund-rate pool into a DAF-rate pool
conclusion_affected: Whether the realised pool ($38.5m–$61.5m) or the schedule pool ($89.9m) is the better CF central
rationale: Realised rates are fee income ÷ total assets for all funds; published DAF list rates (150 bps median) are higher, so the gap between $49m and $90m is partly a basis difference, not over-pricing in the schedules

question: Non-CF tail fee read beyond the census sample: run the same 990 fee-line read on all 599 non-CF tail sponsors ($3.08bn), stratified by category, to estimate the share showing any fee revenue (21% in the 29-sponsor sample vs 71% of census CFs) with a usable confidence interval
conclusion_affected: Whole-tail realised pool: $49.4m (non-CFs zero) to $74.3m (non-CFs at CF rate)
rationale: The non-CF test rests on 29 sponsors holding $173m of $3.08bn; 6 show a fee line and none is classifiable as an internal DAF fee. The script already takes any EIN list

question: Read the fee base of the four non-CF sponsors with large fee lines: National Boy Scouts of America Foundation ('Admin Fees' $5.15m FY2022-24), United Methodist Foundation of Louisiana ('Trustee Management Fees' $3.11m), United Way of the Mid-Willamette Valley ('Administrative Fees' $428k), Educational Foundation ('FEE INCOME' $372k); from Schedule O, audits or fee policies, say whether DAFs are charged and at what rate
conclusion_affected: Whether religious/single-issue sponsors charge DAFs CF-type prices
rationale: These are the only non-CF fee lines of size in the sample; their base (trusts, local council endowments, agency funds) is unstated, so they cannot yet count as DAF fee evidence

question: Propagate the realised-rate pool: replace the floor-type $62.9m (8 CFs) in b4501-04, direction-long-tail-sponsors and strategic-synthesis with the 641-CF realised pool (central $49.4m, band-IQR range $38.5m–$61.5m, bootstrap 90% $42.9m–$58.0m, all-fund basis) and state that the non-CF half of the $138m whole-tail central is not supported by realised evidence
conclusion_affected: Tail fee pool figures in synthesis docs
rationale: The 8-CF median (103 bps) applied flat overstates the pool relative to a size-banded read: the $10m–50m DAF band, which holds 80% of tail CF DAF assets, realises 73 bps
